question: During a lab meeting on big-O notation, which assertion is right?
options: Big-O gives the exact running time in seconds.
An O(n squared) algorithm beats O(n log n) for large n.
Big-O describes growth rates up to constant factors.
gold_answer: Big-O describes growth rates up to constant factors.
notes: Team-authored original item on big-O notation. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: An O(n squared) algorithm beats O(n log n) for large n.

claims.text: Linear search on n items is O(n).

evidence.text: Scanning each element once performs work proportional to n in the worst case.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage counts work proportional to n, which entails the claim.

claims.text: O(1) means the operation is instantaneous.

evidence.text: Constant time means bounded independently of input size, not zero or instantaneous.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage defines constant time as bounded, not instant, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: All efficient programs share one complexity.

evidence.text: Complexities were catalogued across the algorithm survey.

claims.verdict_rationale: A catalogue cannot show all share one complexity, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Big-O gives the exact running time in seconds.

claims.text: Big-O bounds growth from above asymptotically.

evidence.text: The definition requires the function to stay below a scaled reference beyond some input size.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states the from-above asymptotic bound, which entails the claim.

evidence.text: Big-O applies to any resource, most commonly time, not memory exclusively.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage applies the notation beyond memory, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Notation choice changes the running time.

evidence.text: Measured times were reported with identical code under two notations.

claims.verdict_rationale: Identical code cannot run differently by notation, but the passage does not test the claim, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Big-O describes growth rates up to constant factors.

claims.text: Constant factors are ignored in big-O classification.

evidence.text: Scaling the reference absorbs any constant multiplier, making constants invisible to the notation.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes constants absorbed by scaling, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Lower big-O always means faster for every input.

evidence.text: Hidden constants decide small-input winners; asymptotics govern only large inputs.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage gives small-input counterexamples, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Asymptotics alone select the best program.

evidence.text: Engineering factors were weighed alongside asymptotics in the review.

claims.verdict_rationale: Weighing other factors cannot settle the claim, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
